newsitem.title: GREECE: Solana wants Greece, Turkey to avoid tension.
newsitem.headline: Solana wants Greece, Turkey to avoid tension.

text.p: NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana said on Friday he would try to get feuding members Greece and Turkey to agree on measures to avoid tension before a NATO summit in Madrid in July.
"It is my job to find a way so that both countries agree on that. I will do my best," Solana told reporters after a meeting with Greek government officials in Athens.
A 1988 accord between Athens and Ankara that includes several confidence-building mechanisms, such as suspending military exercises in the summer, will be the basis of the new measures, Solana said.
"We would like as much as possible to move forward in this direction before the summit," he added.
Greece and Turkey came to the brink of war last year over a deserted islet in the eastern Aegean. Hostilities were averted through last-minute U.S. intervention but relations remain tense.
Apart from rights in the Aegean, the two neighbours are also at odds over the divided island of Cyprus and minorities in both countries.
Prime Minister Costas Simitis said that Greece saw the 1988 accord as setting guiding principles that could form the basis for further communication.
"These are the general principles on which communication should be eventually based," Simitis told reporters.
